name: North America
title: Great Lakes from ISS
description: The Great Lakes region is clearly visible from the ISS Cupola. Astronauts observe the interconnected freshwater lakes that hold about 21% of the world's surface fresh water. Stunning views show sediment patterns, urban development, and the intricate coastlines of these massive inland seas.
observations: Sediment plume patterns in the water
naturalEvents: Aurora Borealis visible in northern regions, lake-effect snow

name: Amazon Rainforest
title: Amazon Basin
description: The vast Amazon rainforest appears as a lush green expanse from the ISS. The winding Amazon River and its tributaries create stunning patterns across South America.

name: Sahara Desert
title: Sahara Desert from ISS
description: The Sahara's endless golden sand dunes create mesmerizing patterns visible from space. From the ISS Cupola, astronauts witness the vast expanse of one of Earth's most extreme environments. Dark patches indicate ancient lake beds and geological features hidden beneath the sand.
observations: Massive sand dune patterns and formations
naturalEvents: Dust storms transport Saharan sand across Atlantic to Amazon

name: Himalayas
title: Himalayan Mountain Range from ISS
description: The snow-capped peaks of the Himalayas are breathtaking from the ISS. The world's highest mountains create dramatic shadows and patterns. Home to Mount Everest and eight of the world's ten highest peaks, these mountains form a natural barrier between the Indian subcontinent and the Tibetan Plateau.
observations: Snow-covered peaks reaching into the atmosphere

name: Great Barrier Reef
title: Great Barrier Reef from Space
description: The world's largest coral reef system is spectacularly visible from space, appearing as stunning turquoise and blue patterns in the deep ocean off Australia's coast. This natural wonder stretches over 2,300 kilometers and is one of the few living structures visible from orbit.
observations: Intricate coral reef structures in bright blues
Lighter patches indicating shallow reef areas
naturalEvents: Coral bleaching monitoring area, marine biodiversity hotspot

name: Antarctica
title: Antarctic Ice Sheets - Satellite View
description: The vast expanse of Antarctica's ice sheets creates a stunning false-color visualization from space. The continent holds 90% of the world's ice and 70% of its fresh water. This enhanced satellite imagery reveals the complex flow patterns of glaciers and ice streams in vibrant colors.
observations: Ice flow patterns visualized in false color
Massive ice shelf formations along coast
Sea ice extent and seasonal variations
naturalEvents: Aurora Australis displays, ice calving events, katabatic winds
